claims.why: Agitates the sensor to remove bubbles from its optical surface. Uses up-and-down or circular movement to dislodge the bubbles. Activates the wiper mechanism if available.
Explains that bubbles can bias apparent turbidity upward.

Requires at least three sequential readings for the in situ procedure. Requires at least five sequential readings for the flow-through chamber procedure. Takes readings at regular time increments. Requires the sequence to be within 10 percent.
Allows at least 2 minutes before recording the required sequence. Notes that some instruments need 10 to 20 minutes of warmup.
Reports the median of the sequential readings meeting the stability criterion.
Explains that dynamic measurement avoids particle-settling problems in discrete samples.
Warns that static readings can be biased low when sand or coarse silt is present.
States that a sample settling within 3 to 5 seconds cannot be measured accurately with the static method.
Stores the solution in a dark bottle.
Keeps the solution chilled at 4 degrees Celsius. States that stability is reported for at least 90 days under that chilled condition.
Warns that ZoBell's solution is toxic and must be handled with care.
Warns that ZoBell's reacts readily with minute iron particles and dust.
Uses a fresh aliquot of ZoBell's solution for troubleshooting the electrode reading.
Moves the sensor up and down or in a circular pattern to remove bubbles. Activates the wiper if available.
Identifies bubbles as a source of positive turbidity bias.
Uses five or more sequential readings for the flow-through chamber. Spaces the readings at regular time increments. Requires the readings to be within 10 percent.
Treats 2 minutes as the minimum wait before the sequence. Notes that some instruments require 10 to 20 minutes of warmup.
Reports the median of the accepted sequential readings rather than their maximum.
Identifies bubbles as a possible source of positive turbidity bias.
Cleans sensors according to the manufacturer's instructions. Replaces a damaged sensor. Recalibrates after replacing a damaged sensor.
Warns that different turbidity instrument designs commonly do not yield equivalent results.
States that relations between instrument types are site specific.
Preserves instrument design and reporting units when storing turbidity data.
Moves the turbidity sensor up and down or in a circle to dislodge optical-surface bubbles. Activates the wiper mechanism if available.
States that bubbles can produce positive turbidity bias.
